PDF to PowerPoint

Turn a highlighted textbook chapter into a lecture deck

Highlighted passages decide what goes on the slides. Figures, equations and tables stay as exact pictures from the PDF, and your university template is followed to the letter.

  • Runs in this browser
  • Free AI options, or none at all
  • Your .pptx template: logo, fonts, layouts

1Textbook chapter (PDF)

The PDF stays in your browser. Highlights are detected from the page colours (yellow, green, orange by default), so flattened or annotated PDFs both work.

Drop a PDF here or click to choose a file
Analysis options
Highlight colours

2Detected content

Check what was found. Click a picture or a page number to correct a crop, change its type, or add a missed figure or equation. Unticked items are ignored.

3Create the slides

Pick an AI service to write the slides from your chapter. Several are free (a free key, a model on your own computer, or one inside this browser). Or press “Build outline without AI”: it needs nothing and uses only the headings and highlighted sentences.

More settings

4Template

Slides are written as real PowerPoint slides on the template’s own layouts, so its logo, fonts, colours and decorations are used exactly — nothing is re-drawn.

5Review and edit

Change anything before exporting. The preview uses the real layout geometry of your template (background art and exact fonts appear in PowerPoint).

Pop quiz

Questions appear on a “Pop quiz” slide and the answers on the following slide.

6Export

Look through every slide first, exactly as it will be exported. The file is built here in your browser, nothing is uploaded. The quiz page and the notes can be shared on their own.
